content:
Let \(x=\log_3 b\). Then \(\log_{1/3}(b)=-x\).

We have
\[
A(x)=\log_a(\sqrt{x^2+1}+x),\qquad B(x)=\frac1{a^x-1}.
\]
Since
\[
(\sqrt{x^2+1}+x)(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x)=1,
\]
we get
\[
A(-x)=\log_a(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x)=-\log_a(\sqrt{x^2+1}+x)=-A(x).
\]
Also,
\[
B(-x)=\frac1{a^{-x}-1}=-\frac{a^x}{a^x-1}=-1-\frac1{a^x-1}=-1-B(x).
\]
Given \(f(x)=5\):
\[
A(x)+B(x)+\frac32=5 \implies A(x)+B(x)=\frac72.
\]
Thus
\[
f(-x)=A(-x)+B(-x)+\frac32
=-A(x)-1-B(x)+\frac32
=-(A(x)+B(x))+\frac12.
\]
So
\[
f(-x)=-\frac72+\frac12=-3.
\]
\[
\boxed{-3}
\]
